title: PDRN Eye Cream
intro: PDRN eye cream combines K-beauty's favorite fibroblast-activating ingredient with the under-eye area's biggest needs: smoothing fine lines, reducing puffiness, and brightening dark circles. Our vegan formulation pairs Acetyl Tetrapeptide-5 peptides with our non-salmon PDRN serum for a complete Korean-inspired under-eye routine.

body_modules.heading: The under-eye concerns PDRN is known for
body_modules.html:
For moms running on five hours of sleep, the under-eye area tells the whole story. Persistent dark circles that no amount of rest seems to fully reverse. Morning puffiness that lingers past 9am. And the fine lines that started appearing in the outer corners — crow's feet that weren't there two years ago, now visible in every Zoom call. These aren't vanity concerns. They're the visible record of the season you're in, and they deserve actives that actually address them rather than just mask them.

PDRN is the clean-beauty active that uniquely addresses all three. As a polynucleotide that supports fibroblast activity, it helps rebuild the structural integrity of the thin, delicate skin beneath the eye — the same layer responsible for the hollowed, shadowed look that reads as fatigue. Paired with a decongestant peptide to address puffiness and a caffeine-infused gel-cream base, PDRN becomes the under-eye treatment the crunchy-mom market has needed: clinical in mechanism, clean in sourcing, and honest about what it can and can't do.

body_modules.heading: How peptides + PDRN work together under the eye
body_modules.html:
Acetyl Tetrapeptide-5 for puffiness

Acetyl Tetrapeptide-5 is a biomimetic peptide that works through two complementary pathways: it reduces capillary permeability (limiting the fluid leakage that causes morning puffiness) and inhibits glycation-related cross-linking that stiffens the delicate tissue below the eye. The result is a visible decongesting effect over continued use — not a temporary tightening like caffeine alone, but a structural improvement in how the periorbital zone manages fluid. For moms dealing with chronic morning puffiness, this peptide mechanism matters.

PDRN for fine lines and fibroblast support

The eye area has fewer oil glands, less subcutaneous fat, and thinner dermis than the rest of the face — which is why fine lines form here first and why most standard serums are too heavy or too active to use close to the eye. PDRN works here because it's a fibroblast-signaling ingredient, not a resurfacing one. Rather than thinning or stripping the skin, it supports collagen synthesis at the cellular level, helping the under-eye dermis rebuild density and resilience. Non-salmon-derived in our formulation. Same bioactive pathway — no fish origin.

Light gel-cream texture that absorbs without migration into the eye

Eye-area texture isn't cosmetic preference — it's a functional requirement. Heavy creams migrate into the eye during the night, causing irritation by morning. Oil-rich formulas can cause milia along the lash line. Our Peptide Eye Gel-Cream uses a lightweight gel-cream base designed to absorb within 60 seconds of application, staying exactly where you pat it without traveling. The non-comedogenic, fragrance-free base means no sensitization risk for contact lens wearers or those with reactive eyes. A formula that performs beautifully in a lab test but irritates real eyes every morning isn't a good eye cream.

body_modules.heading: Your AM + PM under-eye routine
body_modules.html:
Apply the Peptide Eye Gel-Cream after your PDRN Brightening Serum — always serum first, eye cream second. Use your ring finger to apply; it exerts the least pressure on the delicate periorbital skin. Pat, never rub.

  1. AM — Cleanse: Splash with lukewarm water or use a gentle, low-pH cleanser. Pat face dry with a clean towel — no rubbing the eye area.
  2. AM — PDRN Brightening Serum (face): Apply 2–4 pumps of the Vegan PDRN Brightening Serum to your full face and neck. Allow 30–60 seconds for absorption before moving to the eye step.
  3. AM — Peptide Eye Gel-Cream: Dispense a pea-sized amount. Using your ring finger, pat gently along the orbital bone — starting from the inner corner and moving outward. Do not drag. Allow to absorb fully before applying SPF.
  4. AM — Moisturizer + SPF: Apply your moisturizer, then a broad-spectrum SPF 30+ over the full face. Neither PDRN nor Acetyl Tetrapeptide-5 causes photosensitivity, but daily SPF is essential for any dark-circle or brightening routine.
  5. PM — Cleanse: Remove makeup and SPF thoroughly. Double-cleanse if needed. Pat the eye area dry gently — never rub.
  6. PM — PDRN Serum → Peptide Eye Gel-Cream → Night Cream: Repeat steps 2 and 3. Follow with your overnight moisturizer or a richer barrier cream to seal the actives in. PDRN does its deepest fibroblast-signaling work while you sleep — this step is worth protecting.

body_modules.heading: What we left out
body_modules.html:
The skin around your eyes is the thinnest, most reactive skin on your face. That constraint shaped every formulation decision for the Peptide Eye Gel-Cream. Here's what this formula deliberately excludes:

  • No fragrance — synthetic or natural. Fragrance around the eye area is an unnecessary sensitization risk. Even "clean" essential oils like lavender or chamomile can cause irritation to the delicate orbital tissue.
  • No essential oils — common in natural skincare, but a significant allergen risk in the periorbital zone. Eucalyptus, tea tree, bergamot, and similar oils are out entirely.
  • No harsh preservatives — we avoid formaldehyde-releasing preservatives (DMDM hydantoin, quaternium-15, imidazolidinyl urea) that are disproportionately sensitizing near the eye. Our preservative system uses lower-irritation options at minimal effective concentrations.
  • No retinol — powerful for the face, but not recommended for the under-eye without careful titration. PDRN achieves fibroblast support without the irritation risk.
  • No parabens, sulfates, PEGs, or phthalates — standard Leaf & Bird formulation rules.

We'd rather have an eye cream that does nothing dramatic than one that irritates eyes, causes milia, or leaves you waking up to chemical burn from overnight migration. Every omission on this list was a deliberate choice for the specific vulnerability of the under-eye environment.

faq_json.question: Can I use this if I have sensitive eyes or wear contact lenses?
faq_json.answer: Yes — the Peptide Eye Gel-Cream is formulated with the periorbital zone in mind, which means fragrance-free, essential-oil-free, and no harsh preservatives. For contact lens wearers specifically: apply the eye cream before inserting lenses in the morning, and allow it to fully absorb before lens insertion. If you have a history of extreme eye sensitivity or allergic conjunctivitis, patch-test behind the ear before applying to the eye area. Nothing in this formula is a known contact-lens contraindication, but individual sensitivities vary.

faq_json.question: How close to the lash line should I apply?
faq_json.answer: Apply along the orbital bone — the bony ridge that surrounds the eye socket — rather than directly to the lash line or the eyelid. Pat from the inner corner outward, following the lower orbital bone, and then across the outer corner toward the upper brow bone if desired. Avoid the upper eyelid unless your eye cream is specifically formulated for it. The ingredient actives migrate inward over time; you don't need to place it directly on the lash line to reach that area. Staying on the bone also reduces migration into the eye overnight.

faq_json.question: Does this work for dark circles caused by genetics vs. sleep deprivation?
faq_json.answer: It depends on the type of dark circles. Sleep-related dark circles are largely vascular — caused by dilated capillaries and fluid pooling — and respond well to Acetyl Tetrapeptide-5 (which reduces capillary permeability) and caffeine (a temporary vasoconstrictor). Genetic or structural dark circles — caused by thin skin over blood vessels, or hollow tear troughs — respond better to PDRN's fibroblast-building effect over time, as building dermal density reduces the visual depth of hollows. Pigmentation-based circles (common in deeper skin tones) are a different mechanism and respond best to brightening actives beyond what this formula targets. Most people have a combination — so consistent use over 8–12 weeks gives the most accurate read on your specific circle type.

faq_json.question: Can I use it with mascara or eyeliner?
faq_json.answer: Yes, with sequencing. Apply the Peptide Eye Gel-Cream as part of your skincare routine before makeup — allow it to fully absorb (about 60 seconds) before applying primer, concealer, or eye makeup. Eye cream should never be applied over mascara or liner. In the evening, fully remove all eye makeup before cleansing and applying the eye cream. A thorough but gentle makeup remover is important for the under-eye area — the mechanical rubbing required to remove stubborn mascara is more damaging to the periorbital skin than most people realize.

faq_json.question: Is this eye cream safe during pregnancy?
faq_json.answer: We always recommend consulting your OB or midwife before adding any new active to your pregnancy skincare routine. The Peptide Eye Gel-Cream does not contain retinol, retinoids, salicylic acid, or hydroquinone — the actives most commonly flagged in pregnancy. It does contain peptides and phenoxyethanol as a preservative (at low, EWG-accepted concentrations). Many of our customers use it throughout pregnancy, but the decision belongs to you and your provider.

faq_json.question: How much product should I use?
faq_json.answer: A pea-sized amount covers both eyes. More product does not mean more results — the actives absorb to their maximum depth regardless of volume, and over-applying can increase the chance of migration into the eye area. A single pump or a pea-sized scoop from the jar is the right amount. If you're finding the formula pills under concealer, you're likely applying too much — reduce the amount and allow longer absorption time before makeup application.

faq_json.question: Does the peptide fight the same things as PDRN, or do they work differently?
faq_json.answer: They work through different mechanisms but address overlapping concerns — which is exactly why they're paired. Acetyl Tetrapeptide-5 specifically targets puffiness by reducing capillary fluid permeability: it works at the vascular level in the periorbital tissue. PDRN works deeper — it's a polynucleotide that supports fibroblast activity and collagen synthesis, addressing the structural thinning that causes fine lines and the hollow look that reads as dark circles. Think of the peptide as the decongester and PDRN as the rebuilder. Together they address the under-eye from two separate biological angles.
